requirement:
The first search result delivered in each agent conversation MUST include an
`instructions` string, even when `matches` is empty. Text and structural
searches share this rule. Failed searches leave the instructions for the first
successful delivery. Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.
The instructions explain when to call `finish_search` and which tags to include
in `used`, as described in {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.mcp.description`.

behavioral: The test `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot]` carries a `{test}` marker for `requirements.sdk.graph.search.first_search.instructions`. It covers each obligation in the text:

- **First result has an `instructions` string, even when `matches` is empty.** The first successful `search_text` for `absent` in `session` returns empty matches. The test reads `instructions` with `as_str().unwrap()`, so it must be a string. The first `search_structure` in `peer` also has empty matches. It asserts `page["instructions"] == instructions`. The `fresh` session's first search, `hit`, has matches. The test asserts `hits["instructions"] == instructions`.
- **Text and structural searches share the rule.** The first search is a text search in `session` and `fresh`, and a structural search in `peer`. Each has instructions. In `peer`, a later `search_text` after the structural search omits the field, so the delivery state is shared across the two search types.
- **Failed searches leave the instructions for the first successful delivery.** `session` first runs `search_text` with the invalid pattern `(`, which errors. The next successful search, `absent`, still carries the instructions.
- **Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.** The test asserts the field is absent in each of these cases:
  - The second search in `session` (`hit`).
  - The `get_next_page` result in `fresh`.
  - The `peer` text search after its first structural search.
  - The `get_next_page` result in `session`.
- **Per conversation.** Three separate sessions (`session`, `fresh`, `peer`) each receive instructions on their own first successful search.
- **Content.** The test checks that the instructions contain phrases about when to call `finish_search`, which tags to include in `used`, and `used:[]` for empty results. The wording itself falls under `first_search.instructions.content`, and this subject only cites `finish_search.mcp.description` as context.

There is no explicit test that a failed structural search leaves the instructions for the next success. The text-search failure case and the shared delivery state cover that rule, and the text does not distinguish it. I found no gap.

text: The first search result delivered in each agent conversation MUST include an
`instructions` string, even when `matches` is empty. Text and structural
searches share this rule. Failed searches leave the instructions for the first
successful delivery. Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.
The instructions explain when to call `finish_search` and which tags to include
> `Close a delivered search and record dependencies for snippets you used to
> justify your conclusion without an additional source read. search_id is the
> result's UUID and used is an array of its short entry tags, e.g.
> whose source you also read may be omitted; including them is harmless. Use
> used:[] when no entries qualify, including an empty search. Every delivered
> search must be finished before submission. The result is {search_id,
> finished:true}; no additional source is delivered.`
